1.1: This the record of Jesus Christ's family—He the Son of David, the Son of Abraham.
1.2: Abraham had Isaac, Isaac had Jacob, and Jacob had Judah and his brothers.
1.3: Judah had Perez and Zerah with Tamar, Perez had Hezron, and Hezron had Ram.
1.4: Ram had Amminadab, Amminadab had Nahshon, and Nahshon had Salmon.
1.5: Salmon had Boaz with Rahab, Boaz had Obed with Ruth, and Obed had Jesse.
1.6: Jesse had David—the king. David had Solomon with Uriah's wife.
1.7: Solomon had Rehoboam, Rehoboam had Abijah, and Abijah had Asa.
1.8: Asa had Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat had Joram, and Joram had Uzziah.
1.9: Uzziah had Jotham, Jotham had Ahaz, and Ahaz had Hezekiah.
1.10: Hezekiah had Manasseh, Manasseh had Amon, and Amon had Josiah.
1.11: Josiah had Jeconiah and his brothers around the time they got taken to Babylon.
1.12: After the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah had Shealtiel, and Shealtiel had Zerubbabel.
1.13: Zerubbabel had Abiud, Abiud had Eliakim, and Eliakim had Azor.
1.14: Azor had Zadok, Zadok had Achim, and Achim had Eliud.
1.15: Eliud had Eleazar, Eleazar had Matthan, and Matthan had Jacob.
1.16: Jacob had Joseph, the husband of Mary—and Mary gave birth to Jesus, who's called the Christ.
1.17: So from Abraham to David was 14 generations, from David to the exile was 14, and from the exile to Christ was another 14.
1.18: This how Jesus the Messiah was born: Mary, His mom, was engaged to Joseph. But before they came together, she got pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
1.19: Joseph, her fiancé, was a good dude. He ain't wanna embarrass her, so he planned to call off the engagement on the low.
1.20: But while he was wrestlin' with it, boom—an angel from the Lord showed up in a dream and said, "Joseph, son of David, don't be scared to take Mary as your wife. What's inside her came from the Holy Spirit.
1.21: She gon' have a son, and you gon' name Him Jesus—'cause He gon' save His people from their sins."
1.22: All this went down to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:
1.23: "Look, the virgin gon' be pregnant and give birth to a son, and they gon' call Him Immanuel"—which means "God with us."
1.24: When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel told him. He married Mary,
1.25: but he didn't sleep with her 'til after she had her firstborn son. And he named Him Jesus.

2.1: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem, back when King Herod was in charge, some wise men from the East showed up in Jerusalem.
2.2: They was askin', "Where the newborn King of the Jews at? We saw His star way out East and came to worship Him."
2.3: Herod heard that and got shook—and the whole city felt the tension too.
2.4: He called in all the chief priests and Bible experts and asked, "Where the Messiah supposed to be born?"
2.5: They told him, "Bethlehem, in Judea—just like the prophet said:
2.6: 'You, Bethlehem in Judah, ain't the least outta all Judah's towns. Outta you gon' come a Ruler who gon' lead My people Israel like a shepherd.'"
2.7: Then Herod pulled the wise men to the side on the low, tryna figure out exactly when the star popped up.
2.8: He told them, "Go find that child real careful. When y'all find Him, come back and let me know, so I can worship Him too." (Yeah, aight.)
2.9: After they left, the same star they saw earlier showed back up and guided them 'til it stopped right over the place where Jesus was.
2.10: When they saw that star, they turned up with serious joy—like, over-the-top rejoicin'.
2.11: They stepped in the house, saw the child with His mama Mary, dropped to their knees, and worshiped Him. Then they opened up their treasure chests and brought out gifts—gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
2.12: But God came through in a dream and told 'em not to go back to Herod. So they dipped back to their country takin' a whole different route.
2.13: Soon as they left, boom—an angel of the Lord showed up in Joseph's dream: "Get up, take the child and His mama, and run to Egypt. Stay there 'til I tell you, 'cause Herod lookin' for the boy and tryna kill Him."
2.14: Joseph got up that night, packed up Mary and baby Jesus, and they headed to Egypt.
2.15: They stayed there until Herod died. That fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: "I called My Son outta Egypt."
2.16: Herod realized the wise men played him—dude was heated. So he sent people to kill every baby boy in Bethlehem and the surrounding area, two years old and under—based on the timeline he got from the wise men.
2.17: That right there fulfilled what the prophet Jeremiah had said:
2.18: "A voice cried out in Ramah, weeping and heartbreak, Rachel cryin' for her kids. She wouldn't be comforted, 'cause they gone."
2.19: After Herod died, the angel of the Lord pulled up again in Joseph's dream while they was still in Egypt.
2.20: He said, "Get up, take the child and His mama, and go back to Israel. The folks who wanted the boy dead—they gone."
2.21: So Joseph got up, took Mary and Jesus, and went back to Israel.
2.22: But when he heard that Herod's son Archelaus was running things in Judea, he got nervous. Then God warned him in another dream, so he switched it up and headed for Galilee.
2.23: They ended up living in a town called Nazareth. That fulfilled the prophets too: "He gon' be called a Nazarene."

3.1: Back in those days, John the Baptist pulled up preachin' in the wilderness of Judea.
3.2: He was hollerin', "Y'all better repent, 'cause the Kingdom of Heaven is right around the corner!"
3.3: This him—the one Isaiah was talkin' 'bout when he said: "A voice shoutin' in the wild: Make the Lord's path ready, Clear the road for Him to come through."
3.4: John had on camel hair with a leather belt, and bruh was munchin' on locusts and wild honey.
3.5: Folks from Jerusalem, all over Judea, and around the Jordan was comin' out to hear him.
3.6: And when they came, they confessed their sins and got baptized by him in the Jordan River.
3.7: But when John saw the Pharisees and Sadducees steppin' up to get baptized, he called 'em out: "Y'all some snakes! Who warned y'all to run from what's comin'?
3.8: If you really tryna repent, show it—live right. Bear fruit that matches the change.
3.9: And don't act like you good just 'cause Abraham your ancestor. I'm tellin' y'all, God can raise up Abraham's kids from these rocks.
3.10: The ax is already sittin' at the root of the trees. Any tree not producing good fruit? It's gettin' chopped down and tossed in the fire."
3.11: "I'm baptizin' y'all with water so you can turn from sin, but somebody way greater than me is comin'. I'm not even worthy to carry His sandals. He gon' baptize y'all with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
3.12: He got His winnowing fork ready—He gon' clean up His threshing floor, gather the wheat in the barn, and burn up the chaff with a fire that don't quit."
3.13: Then Jesus came down from Galilee to the Jordan to get baptized by John.
3.14: But John tried to stop Him: "Wait—I need to get baptized by You, and You comin' to me?"
3.15: But Jesus said, Let it happen for now. We gotta do this to fulfill what's right in God's eyes. So John was like, "Bet," and baptized Him.
3.16: Soon as Jesus came up out that water, the skies opened up, and He saw God's Spirit comin' down like a dove and landin' on Him.
3.17: Then a voice boomed from heaven: "That's My Son right there—the one I love. He bring Me so much joy."

4.1: Then the Spirit led Jesus out into the wilderness, so the devil could test Him.
4.2: He ain't eat nothin' for forty days and forty nights. After that? Yeah, He was hungry hungry.
4.3: So here come the tempter talkin' slick: "If You really the Son of God, go 'head and tell these stones to turn into bread."
4.4: But Jesus clapped back, "Nah, it's written—Man don't live off bread alone, but off every word that come from God's mouth."
4.5: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and posted Him up on the highest point of the temple.
4.6: He said, "If You the Son of God, jump! Ain't it written, 'God gon' tell His angels to look out for You,' and 'They gon' catch You so You don't even stub your toe'?"
4.7: Jesus said, "It's also written: Don't play with the Lord your God."
4.8: So Satan tried one more time—took Jesus to a crazy high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their shine.
4.9: He said, "All this could be Yours if You just bow down and worship me."
4.10: Jesus shut it down: "Get outta here, Satan! It's written—Worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only."
4.11: So the devil dipped, and right then, angels showed up and took care of Jesus.
4.12: When Jesus heard John had got locked up, He headed back to Galilee.
4.13: He left Nazareth and moved to Capernaum, by the sea, in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali.
4.14: This was to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah had said:
4.15: "Land of Zebulun and Naphtali, by the sea, past the Jordan, Galilee where the outsiders live—
4.16: The people sittin' in the dark seen a big light. Those sittin' in the shadow of death, light done broke through."
4.17: From that point on, Jesus started preachin' loud and clear: "Change how you livin'—God's kingdom is right here!"
4.18: Jesus was walkin' by the Sea of Galilee when He spotted two brothers—Simon (also called Peter) and Andrew. They was out there tossin' nets in the water 'cause they were fishermen.
4.19: Jesus told 'em, "Come follow Me, and I'll teach y'all how to catch people instead."
4.20: They dropped they nets right then and followed Him.
4.21: He kept it movin' and saw two more brothers—James and John, sons of Zebedee. They was in the boat with they daddy, fixin' nets. Jesus called them too.
4.22: They ain't even hesitate—left the boat, left they pops, and rolled with Jesus.
4.23: Jesus was all over Galilee, teachin' in the synagogues, preachin' the Good News about the kingdom, and healin' folks from every kind of sickness and disease.
4.24: Word got out quick—folks from Syria and everywhere else started bringin' the sick to Him: folks with diseases, pain, demons, seizures, and folks who couldn't walk. Jesus healed every last one.
4.25: Big crowds followed Him—from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and across the Jordan too.

5.1: When Jesus saw the crowd pull up, He went up on a mountain. After He sat down, His disciples came through.
5.2: Then Jesus started speakin', teachin' them like this:
5.3: "Blessed are the ones who know they need God—'cause heaven already belong to them.
5.4: Blessed are the ones who hurt and grieve—'cause God gon' comfort them.
5.5: Blessed are the humble and gentle—'cause they gon' inherit the whole earth.
5.6: Blessed are the ones who crave righteousness like food and water—'cause they gon' be filled up.
5.7: Blessed are the ones who show mercy—'cause they gon' get mercy too.
5.8: Blessed are the ones with pure hearts—'cause they gon' see God for real.
5.9: Blessed are the peacemakers—'cause they gon' be known as God's children.
5.10: Blessed are the ones gettin' hated on for doin' right—'cause the kingdom of heaven theirs.
5.11: And blessed are y'all when people talk reckless about you, lie on you, and come at you sideways just 'cause you rockin' with Me.
5.12: Don't trip—rejoice! Be hype! Your reward up in heaven gon' be major. They did the same thing to the prophets before y'all."
5.13: "Y'all the salt of the earth. But if salt lose its flavor, what's the point? It ain't good for nothin' but gettin' tossed out and stepped on.
5.14: Y'all the light of the world. A city up on a hill can't be hidden.
5.15: Nobody lights a lamp just to put it under a bucket—they put it on a stand so it can light up the whole room.
5.16: So let your light shine in front of everybody, so they can see your good deeds and give props to your Father in heaven."
5.17: "Don't get it twisted—don't think I came to cancel the Law or the Prophets. I ain't come to erase it—I came to fulfill it.
5.18: Truth is, not even a period or comma from the law gon' fade 'til everything is complete.
5.19: Anybody who breaks the smallest command and teaches others to do the same? They gon' be the least in the kingdom. But the ones who live it and teach it? They gon' be great in the kingdom.
5.20: I'm tellin' y'all: unless your righteousness go beyond that of the Pharisees and law teachers, you not even gettin' in the kingdom."
5.21: "Y'all heard the rule: 'Don't kill nobody. If you do, you face judgment.'
5.22: But I'm tellin' you: if you mad at your brother for no reason, you already in danger. And if you call them names like 'Raca' (basically, 'idiot') or 'Fool,' you headin' toward serious judgment—even hellfire.
5.23: So if you about to bring your offering to God, and you remember your brother got beef with you?
5.24: Leave your gift. Go make it right with them first. Then come back and give your gift.
5.25: If somebody takin' you to court, squash the drama before y'all even get there. 'Cause if not, they might hand you over to the judge, and next thing you know—you in jail.
5.26: I'm tellin' you straight: You not gettin' out until every last penny is paid."
5.27: "Y'all heard it said, 'Don't cheat—don't commit adultery.'
5.28: But I'm sayin': if you look at someone with lust, you already committed adultery in your heart.
5.29: If your right eye got you wildin'—pluck it out. It's better to lose one part than your whole body get tossed in hell.
5.30: If your right hand keep messin' you up—cut it off. Better to lose that than your whole body get thrown into hell."
5.31: "They said, 'If you divorce your wife, give her a certificate.'
5.32: But I'm sayin': if you divorce her for anything other than cheating, you makin' her commit adultery—and whoever marries her? Same deal."
5.33: "Y'all heard: 'Don't swear falsely. Keep your vows to God.'
5.34: But I say: don't swear at all. Not by heaven—it's God's throne.
5.35: Not by earth—that's His footstool. Not by Jerusalem—that's His city.
5.36: Don't even swear on your own head—you can't make a single hair white or black.
5.37: Just say 'Yes' or 'No.' Anything more than that? That's the enemy talkin'."
5.38: "Y'all heard, 'Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth.'
5.39: But I say: don't clap back on evil folks. If somebody slap you on one cheek, offer the other one too.
5.40: If they sue you for your shirt, give 'em your coat too.
5.41: If they force you to walk a mile, walk two.
5.42: If somebody ask you for somethin', give it. If they try to borrow, don't turn 'em away."
5.43: "Y'all heard, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
5.44: But I'm tellin' you: Love your enemies. Bless the ones talkin' crazy. Do good to the ones that hate you. Pray for the ones who use you and persecute you.
5.45: That's how you show you belong to your Father in heaven. He makes the sun rise on both the good and the bad. Sends rain to the righteous and the unrighteous.
5.46: If you only love the folks who love you, what's special about that? Even tax collectors do that.
5.47: And if you only speak to your crew, what makes you different?
5.48: So be mature, be whole—just like your Father in heaven is.

6.1: Don't be out here showin' off your good deeds just to get seen by folks. If you do, don't expect no reward from your Father in heaven.
6.2: When you give to folks in need, don't be blowin' it up like a trumpet like them fake folks in church and on the streets tryna look holy. I'm tellin' you—they already got they reward.
6.3: But when you give, keep it lowkey—don't even let your left hand know what your right hand doin'.
6.4: Do your givin' in secret, and your Father—who sees what's done on the low—He gon' bless you in the open.
6.5: When you pray, don't act like the fakes who love to stand and be seen prayin' on corners and in the synagogues. They already got their lil' applause.
6.6: But when you pray, slide into your room, shut the door, and talk to your Father in secret. He sees you—and He gon' bless you for it.
6.7: And don't be prayin' with long, empty talk like folks who don't know God. They think God hear them just 'cause they sayin' a lot.
6.8: Don't be like them—your Father already know what you need before you even ask.
6.9: So when you pray, say: Our Father in heaven, We honor Your name.
6.10: Let Your kingdom come. Let Your will be done—On earth just like it is in heaven.
6.11: Give us today the bread we need.
6.12: Forgive us our debts, As we forgive the folks who owe us.
6.13: Don't lead us into temptation, But rescue us from the evil one. 'Cause the kingdom, the power, and the glory is Yours—forever. Amen.
6.14: If you forgive people for the wrong they did to you, your Father in heaven gon' forgive you too.
6.15: But if you don't forgive them? Don't expect your Father to forgive your mess either.
6.16: When you fast, don't be walkin' around lookin' sad and pitiful like them hypocrites. They do that so folks will know they fastin'. That's all the reward they gon' get.
6.17: But when you fast, wash your face and oil your head—look normal.
6.18: That way, only your Father in secret sees what's up. And He gon' bless you for real.
6.19: Don't be stackin' up treasure here on earth, where moths and rust ruin stuff and thieves break in.
6.20: Stack up treasure in heaven instead—where it can't get messed up or stolen.
6.21: 'Cause wherever your treasure at? That's where your heart gon' be too.
6.22: The eye is like a lamp for your whole body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body full of light.
6.23: But if your eye bad, your whole body full of darkness. And if the "light" in you is really darkness? That's some deep darkness right there.
6.24: You can't serve two bosses. You gon' hate one and love the other, or be loyal to one and despise the other. You can't serve both God and money.
6.25: That's why I'm sayin': don't stress about your life—what you gon' eat, drink, or wear. Life ain't just about food and clothes.
6.26: Look at the birds—they don't plant or harvest or store up food, but God feeds them. Ain't you more valuable than birds?
6.27: Worryin' ain't gon' add one inch to your height or one minute to your life.
6.28: Why worry about clothes? Look at the flowers out in the field—they don't hustle, but they stay lookin' fly.
6.29: Even Solomon, in all his royal drip, ain't look that good.
6.30: If God dresses wildflowers that only last a day, won't He take care of you? C'mon now, have some faith.
6.31: So don't be out here stressin', sayin', "What we gon' eat?" or "What we gon' wear?"
6.32: That's what folks who don't know God worry about. Your Father already know what you need.
6.33: But seek God's kingdom first. Chase after His righteousness. Everything else you need? He gon' add it to you.
6.34: Don't worry 'bout tomorrow—tomorrow got its own problems. Deal with today. That's enough for now.

7.1: Don't be out here judgin' folks, unless you ready to get judged the same way.
7.2: 'Cause however you judge others? That same energy comin' right back to you.
7.3: Why you stressin' about the little speck in your brother's eye, when you got a whole log in your own?
7.4: How you gon' say, "Let me fix your eye," but you walkin' around with a whole plank blockin' your vision?
7.5: You fake for that! Handle your own mess first—take the plank out your own eye—then you'll be able to help your brother with his.
7.6: Don't throw what's sacred to the dogs. Don't toss your pearls to pigs—they'll just stomp on it, then turn around and come for you.
7.7: Ask—and you'll get it. Seek—and you'll find it. Knock—and that door gon' open.
7.8: Everybody who asks, gets. The one who seeks, finds. And if you knock? Yeah, it's gon' open.
7.9: Which one of y'all would give your child a rock if they asked for bread?
7.10: Or a snake if they asked for fish?
7.11: Y'all flawed, and y'all still know how to give good gifts to your kids. So imagine how much more your heavenly Father gon' give to the ones who ask Him!
7.12: So whatever you want folks to do for you? Do that for them. That right there sums up the Law and the Prophets.
7.13: Get in through the narrow gate—'cause the wide one? That's the easy road, but it leads straight to destruction. And a whole lotta folks walkin' that one.
7.14: But the narrow gate? That's the one that leads to life. It ain't easy, and only a few gon' find it.
7.15: Watch out for fake prophets. They come lookin' innocent like sheep, but inside? They straight-up wolves.
7.16: You gon' know them by their fruit. You ever seen grapes growin' from thorns? Or figs from thistles? Nah.
7.17: Every good tree gives good fruit. Bad trees give bad fruit.
7.18: A good tree can't give bad fruit, and a bad tree can't give good fruit.
7.19: Any tree that don't produce good fruit? It's gettin' chopped down and tossed in the fire.
7.20: So yeah—you'll know them by what they produce.
7.21: Not everybody who hollers "Lord, Lord" is gettin' into heaven. Only the ones who do what God wants.
7.22: Plenty gon' say on judgment day: "Lord, didn't we prophesy in Your name? Didn't we cast out demons and do big miracles in Your name?"
7.23: But I'm gon' tell them straight up: "I never knew you. Move around—you out here doin' wrong."
7.24: So if you hear My words and actually do 'em, you like a wise builder who put his house on solid rock.
7.25: The rain came, the flood hit, the wind blew hard—but that house stood tall, 'cause it had a strong foundation.
7.26: But if you hear My words and ignore 'em? You like a fool who built his house on sand.
7.27: The rain came, floods rushed in, wind smacked it—and boom. That house fell hard. And the fall? Yeah, it was major."
7.28: When Jesus finished preachin' all this, the crowd was shook.
7.29: 'Cause He wasn't talkin' like them teachers they was used to. He spoke with real authority—like He knew what He was talkin' about.

8.1: When Jesus came down from the mountain, a huge crowd followed Him.
8.2: Then a man with leprosy pulled up, bowed low, and said, "Lord, if You want to, You can make me clean."
8.3: Jesus reached out, touched him, and said, "I want to. Be clean." And just like that, the man was healed—leprosy gone.
8.4: Jesus told him, "Don't go tellin' everybody. Just go to the priest, show yourself, and give the offering Moses talked about. That's proof for them."
8.5: When Jesus got to Capernaum, a Roman officer came to Him, beggin'.
8.6: He said, "Lord, my servant at home is paralyzed, in bad shape, sufferin' bad."
8.8: But the centurion said, "Lord, I ain't even worthy for You to come in my house. Just say the word and he'll be healed.
8.9: I know how authority works—I got soldiers too. I tell one 'Go' and he go, another 'Come' and he come. I say 'Do this' and it's done."
8.10: When Jesus heard that, He was amazed. He turned to the crowd and said, "Y'all, I ain't seen faith like this—not even in Israel.
8.11: And I'm tellin' you: folks from all over—east, west, everywhere—gon' be chillin' with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in heaven.
8.12: But some of the so-called 'chosen ones' gon' get thrown out into the dark—where there's cryin' and teeth grindin'."
8.13: Then He told the centurion, "Go on. You believed—now it's done." And the servant got healed that same hour.
8.14: When Jesus got to Peter's crib, He saw his wife's mama layin' in bed with a fever.
8.15: He touched her hand, the fever dipped, and she got up and started servin' everybody.
8.16: That evening, folks brought Jesus a bunch of demon-possessed people. He cast the demons out with just one word and healed everybody.
8.17: That fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah said: "He took on our weaknesses and carried our sicknesses."
8.18: When Jesus saw the crowd gettin' thick, He said, "Let's dip to the other side."
8.19: One of the religious teachers came up and said, "Teacher, I'll follow You wherever You go."
8.20: Jesus said, "Foxes got holes, birds got nests, but Me? I ain't even got a place to lay My head."
8.21: Another dude said, "Lord, let me bury my father first."
8.22: Jesus told him, "Follow Me. Let the dead handle the dead."
8.23: Jesus got in a boat and His disciples rode with Him.
8.24: Outta nowhere, a wild storm hit the sea—waves was takin' over the boat. But Jesus? Knocked out sleep.
8.25: The disciples ran to Him like, "Lord! Save us—we 'bout to die!"
8.26: Jesus said, "Why y'all so scared? Where's your faith?" Then He got up, told the wind and waves to chill—and just like that, the sea was calm.
8.27: The disciples were shook. They said, "Who is this man? Even the wind and the sea do what He say!"
8.28: When they got to the other side, in the Gergesenes area, two demon-possessed men came out the tombs. These dudes were wild—nobody even walked that road 'cause of them.
8.29: They yelled out, "What You want with us, Son of God? You here to torment us before the set time?"
8.30: Off in the distance, there was a big herd of pigs.
8.31: The demons begged, "If You gon' cast us out, send us into the pigs."
8.32: Jesus said, "Go." Soon as He said that, they jumped out the men and into the pigs. Then the whole herd ran off the cliff and drowned in the water.
8.33: The folks watchin' the pigs ran off, told the town everything—especially about the demon dudes.
8.34: The whole city came out to see Jesus. But when they saw Him, they begged Him to leave their area.

9.1: Jesus got back in the boat, crossed over, and pulled up in His own town.
9.2: Some folks brought Him a man paralyzed and laid out on a mat. When Jesus saw how strong their faith was, He said, "Son, cheer up—your sins are forgiven."
9.3: That made some of the religious folks mad quiet, thinkin' to themselves, "This man blaspheming!"
9.4: But Jesus knew what they was thinkin'. He said, "Why y'all got evil in your hearts?
9.5: What's easier to say—'Your sins are forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'?
9.6: But to show you I got authority on earth to forgive sins..." He turned to the paralyzed man and said, "Get up, grab your mat, and go home."
9.7: And just like that, the man got up and walked off.
9.8: The crowd was shook and started givin' glory to God, amazed He gave that kind of power to a man.
9.9: As Jesus was movin' along, He saw a dude named Matthew workin' the tax booth. Jesus said, "Follow Me." Matthew got up and did just that.
9.10: Later, Jesus was chillin' at the table in the house, and a bunch of tax collectors and "sinners" came through and sat with Him and His crew.
9.11: When the Pharisees saw all that, they asked Jesus' disciples, "Why your teacher eatin' with folks like that?"
9.12: Jesus heard them and said, "People who healthy don't need a doctor—sick folks do.
9.13: Go learn what this mean: 'I want mercy, not sacrifice.' I didn't come for the ones who think they righteous—I came for the ones who know they messed up."
9.14: Then John's disciples pulled up and asked, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast, but Your crew don't?"
9.15: Jesus said, "Can the wedding guests mourn while the groom still with them? Nah. But one day the groom gon' be taken, and then they gon' fast.
9.16: You don't patch old clothes with new cloth—it just tears up worse.
9.17: And you don't put new wine in old skins. If you do, they'll bust and spill everything. Nah—you put new wine in new skins. That way both stay intact."
9.18: While Jesus was still talkin', a leader came up, bowed down, and said, "My daughter just died. But if You come touch her, she'll live."
9.19: Jesus got up and went with him—and so did His disciples.
9.20: On the way, a woman who'd been bleeding for 12 years came up behind Him and touched His clothes.
9.21: She said to herself, "If I can just touch His robe, I know I'll be healed."
9.22: Jesus turned around, saw her, and said, "Be encouraged, daughter—your faith made you whole." And right then, she got healed.
9.23: When Jesus got to the leader's house, the funeral crowd was already playin' music and cryin' loud.
9.24: He said, "Y'all chill—she not dead, she just sleepin'." They laughed at Him.
9.25: But after He kicked 'em all out, He went in, grabbed the girl's hand—and she got up.
9.26: Word about that miracle spread everywhere.
9.27: As Jesus left, two blind men started followin' Him, shoutin', "Son of David, have mercy on us!"
9.28: When He got in the house, they came inside too. Jesus asked, "Y'all believe I can really do this?" They said, "Yes, Lord."
9.29: Then He touched they eyes and said, "Let it happen based on your faith."
9.30: Their eyes opened just like that. Jesus told 'em, "Keep this on the low."
9.31: But they couldn't keep it quiet—they told everybody.
9.32: As they were leavin', some folks brought Jesus a man who couldn't talk 'cause he had a demon.
9.33: Jesus cast the demon out, and the man started talkin'. The crowd was stunned: "Ain't never seen nothing like this in Israel!"
9.34: But the Pharisees? Haters as usual. They said, "He castin' out demons with demonic power." (Boy, bye.)
9.35: Jesus kept movin'—hittin' up towns and villages, teachin' in synagogues, preachin' that kingdom gospel, and healin' every kind of sickness and disease.
9.36: When He saw the crowd, He was moved deep—'cause they was worn out, lost, and scattered, like sheep with no shepherd.
9.37: He told His disciples, "The harvest out here is huge, but we ain't got enough workers.
9.38: So pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out more laborers to work the field."

10.1: Jesus called His twelve disciples over and gave 'em real power—to cast out demons and heal every kind of sickness and disease.
10.2: Here's who He chose: First, Simon (aka Peter) and his brother Andrew. Then James (Zebedee's son) and John his brother.
10.3: Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, and Matthew (the tax man). James (son of Alphaeus) and Thaddaeus.
10.4: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot—the one who later betrayed Him.
10.5: Jesus sent these twelve out and told them, "Don't go to the Gentiles or the Samaritans just yet.
10.6: Go to the lost sheep of Israel first.
10.7: And when you go, preach this: 'The kingdom of heaven is real close.'
10.8: Heal the sick. Raise the dead. Cleanse lepers. Cast out demons. You got all this for free, so give it out for free.
10.9: Don't take no gold, silver, or change in your pockets.
10.10: Don't pack a travel bag, extra clothes, shoes, or even a walking stick. A worker deserves to be taken care of."
10.11: "When you pull up in a town, find somebody solid to stay with. Stay there the whole time.
10.12: When you enter a house, bless it with peace.
10.13: If they down with you, let your peace rest on them. If not? Take that peace back.
10.14: If they don't welcome you or listen, dust your feet off as you leave that spot.
10.15: I'm tellin' you—the judgment gon' hit that place harder than Sodom and Gomorrah."
10.16: "Listen—I'm sendin' y'all out like sheep among wolves. Be wise like snakes but gentle like doves.
10.17: Watch out for people—they gon' drag y'all into courts and beat y'all in synagogues.
10.18: You gon' be brought before kings and governors 'cause of Me, as a witness to them and the Gentiles.
10.19: But don't stress about what to say. When the time comes, God gon' give you the words.
10.20: It ain't even gon' be you talkin'—it'll be the Spirit of your Father speakin' through you."
10.21: "Families gon' turn on each other. Brothers snitchin'. Parents and kids betrayin' one another.
10.22: You gon' be hated by everybody just 'cause you rock with Me. But if you stay down to the end, you gon' be saved.
10.23: When they come for you in one city, bounce to the next. You won't finish hittin' every town before the Son of Man comes."
10.24: "A student ain't above their teacher. A servant ain't above their master.
10.25: It's enough to be like the teacher. If they called Me Beelzebub, what you think they gon' call you?
10.26: Don't be scared of 'em. Everything in the dark gon' come to light."
10.27: "Whatever I whisper in your ear in the dark? Say it loud in the light. Shout it from the rooftops.
10.28: Don't fear people who can kill your body but can't touch your soul. Fear the One who can destroy both in hell.
10.29: Ain't two sparrows sold for a penny? But not one of 'em falls without your Father knowin'.
10.30: God even got the number of hairs on your head counted.
10.31: So don't be scared—you worth way more than sparrows."
10.32: "If you stand up for Me in front of people, I'll stand up for you in front of My Father in heaven.
10.33: But if you act like you don't know Me? I'll say I don't know you either."
10.34: "Don't get it twisted—I ain't come to bring peace. I came to bring a sword.
10.35: I came to shake things up—even in families.
10.36: Sometimes your biggest haters gon' be the ones in your own house.
10.37: If you love your parents or your kids more than Me? You ain't worthy of Me.
10.38: If you ain't willing to pick up your cross and follow Me? You not worthy either.
10.39: Try to save your life, and you'll lose it. But if you lose your life for Me? You'll find it."
10.40: "If they welcome you, they welcome Me. And if they welcome Me, they welcome the One who sent Me.
10.41: If they bless a prophet, they gon' get a prophet's blessing. If they receive a righteous person, they gon' get that righteous reward too.
10.42: And even if someone gives a cup of cold water to My disciple—just 'cause they My disciple—they won't lose their reward."

11.1: After Jesus finished givin' His twelve disciples instructions, He dipped out and started preachin' and teachin' in their cities.
11.2: Meanwhile, John was locked up in prison. When he heard about all the stuff Jesus was doin', he sent two of his people
11.3: To ask Jesus, "Are You the One we been waitin' for, or should we be lookin' for somebody else?"
11.4: Jesus told 'em, "Go back and tell John what you see and hear:
11.5: Blind folks gettin' their sight. People who couldn't walk now up on they feet. Lepers gettin' cleaned. Deaf folks hearin'. Dead folks raisin' up. And the broke and overlooked? They finally hearin' Good News.
11.6: And blessed is the one who don't trip on Me."
11.7: As John's crew walked off, Jesus started speakin' to the crowd about John: "When y'all went out to the wilderness, what you expect to see? A reed blowin' in the wind?
11.8: Or a man rockin' soft, fancy clothes? Nah—folks like that live in palaces.
11.9: So what did y'all really go out to see? A prophet? Yup—and not just any prophet.
11.10: John the Baptist is the one Scripture was talkin' about: 'Look, I'm sendin' My messenger ahead of You. He gon' prepare the way for You.'
11.11: I'm tellin' y'all straight: Ain't nobody born of a woman greater than John. But even the least person in God's kingdom got it better than him.
11.12: Since John stepped on the scene, the kingdom of heaven been under pressure—and it's the bold and relentless that take hold of it.
11.13: All the prophets and the law pointed to this moment—up until John.
11.14: If y'all really ready to receive it—he is Elijah, the one who was supposed to come.
11.16: "So what can I even compare this generation to? Y'all like kids sittin' outside playin', yellin' to each other:
11.17: 'We played a song, but y'all ain't dance. We cried, but y'all ain't mourn.'
11.18: John came through, not eatin' or drinkin', and y'all said, 'He got a demon.'
11.19: I came through eatin' and drinkin', and y'all said, 'Look at Him—a glutton, a drunk, hangin' with tax collectors and sinners.' But wisdom gon' prove itself right by what it produces."
11.20: Then Jesus started callin' out the cities where He did the most miracles—but they still ain't turn to God.
11.21: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If Tyre and Sidon saw what y'all seen, they would've been repentin' in sackcloth and ashes a long time ago.
11.22: I'm tellin' you—it'll be easier on Tyre and Sidon at judgment time than on y'all.
11.23: And you, Capernaum? You think you all the way up? Nah, you gon' be brought low. If Sodom had seen what y'all seen, it would still be standin'.
11.24: But I'm tellin' you—it'll be better for Sodom than for you on judgment day."
11.25: At that point, Jesus prayed out loud, sayin', "Thank You, Father—Lord of heaven and earth. You kept this hidden from the ones who think they wise and revealed it to the childlike.
11.26: Yes, Father—'cause that's how You wanted it.
11.27: My Father handed everything over to Me. Nobody really knows the Son except the Father. And nobody knows the Father except the Son—and whoever the Son chooses to show Him to.
11.28: So come to Me, all y'all who tired and weighed down—I'll give you rest.
11.29: Take My yoke and learn from Me. I'm gentle and humble, and you'll find real rest for your soul.
11.30: My yoke? It's easy. My burden? Light."

12.1: One Sabbath day, Jesus and His disciples was walkin' through some grainfields. They were hungry, so they started pickin' grain to eat.
12.2: The Pharisees saw it and said, "Look! Your disciples breakin' Sabbath law!"
12.3: But Jesus said, "Y'all ever read what David did when he was hungry—him and his people?
12.4: He went in God's house and ate the holy bread, even though only the priests were allowed to eat it.
12.5: And don't y'all know the Law say priests work on the Sabbath, and they still not guilty?
12.6: But let Me tell you—Someone greater than the temple is right here.
12.7: If y'all really understood what God meant when He said, 'I want mercy, not sacrifice,' you wouldn't be accusin' folks who ain't done nothin' wrong.
12.8: 'Cause the Son of Man is Lord—even over the Sabbath."
12.9: Jesus left there and went to their synagogue.
12.10: A man with a messed-up hand was there. They tried to trap Jesus, askin', "Is it legal to heal on the Sabbath?"
12.11: Jesus said, "If you got one sheep and it fall in a ditch on the Sabbath, you gon' leave it there? Nah, you'll pull it out.
12.12: Ain't a person worth way more than a sheep? So yes—it's right to do good on the Sabbath."
12.13: Then He told the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did, and it got healed—looked just like the other one.
12.14: The Pharisees left mad and started plottin' how to kill Jesus.
12.15: Jesus knew they was comin' for Him, so He dipped out. But big crowds still followed Him—and He healed every last one.
12.16: He told them not to make it public,
12.17: So the prophecy from Isaiah could be fulfilled:
12.18: "Here go My chosen Servant, the One I love. I'll put My Spirit on Him, and He'll bring justice to the Gentiles.
12.19: He won't argue or be loud in the streets.
12.20: He won't crush the weak or snuff out the barely hangin' on—He'll keep bringin' justice until it wins.
12.21: And even the Gentiles gon' put their hope in His name."
12.22: Somebody brought Jesus a man possessed by a demon—he couldn't see or talk. Jesus healed him, and the man started speakin' and seein'.
12.23: Everybody was amazed and said, "Could this really be the Son of David?"
12.24: But the Pharisees said, "He castin' out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons."
12.25: Jesus knew what they were thinkin' and said, "A kingdom divided can't stand.
12.26: If Satan castin' out Satan, he fightin' himself—how his kingdom gon' stand?
12.27: And if I cast demons out by Beelzebub, who your own people cast them out by? Let them judge.
12.28: But if I'm castin' them out by God's Spirit—then the kingdom just pulled up on y'all.
12.29: Ain't nobody robbin' a strong man's house unless they tie him up first. Then they can take what they want.
12.30: If you ain't with Me, you against Me. If you ain't helpin' Me gather, you out here scatterin'."
12.31: "Let Me be clear—every sin and kind of blasphemy can be forgiven. But speakin' against the Holy Spirit? That's the one thing that ain't forgivable.
12.32: Talk trash about Me? You might be forgiven. But talk against the Spirit? That don't get forgiven—not now, not ever."
12.33: "Either the tree good and the fruit good, or the tree bad and the fruit bad. You know the tree by what it grows.
12.34: Y'all snakes! How y'all gon' say anything good when your hearts so foul? What's in the heart comes out the mouth.
12.35: A good heart brings out good things. A bad heart brings out evil.
12.36: And let Me tell y'all—every careless word you say? You gon' answer for it on judgment day.
12.37: By your words, you'll be justified—or condemned."
12.38: Then some of the religious leaders said, "Teacher, give us a sign."
12.39: Jesus said, "This generation so wicked and unfaithful. Always askin' for signs. But the only sign y'all gettin' is the sign of Jonah.
12.40: Just like Jonah was in the belly of the fish for three days and nights, the Son of Man gon' be in the heart of the earth three days and nights.
12.41: The people from Nineveh gon' rise up and call y'all out—'cause they repented when Jonah spoke. And now somebody greater than Jonah is here.
12.42: The Queen of the South gon' rise up and check y'all too—she came from way off just to hear Solomon's wisdom. And y'all got somebody greater than Solomon standin' in front of you."
12.43: "When an evil spirit leaves someone, it be out here wanderin', lookin' for a new place to chill. But if it can't find one,
12.44: It says, 'Let me go back to my old spot.' When it comes back and sees the house cleaned up and empty,
12.45: It brings seven more evil spirits worse than itself, and they all move in. That person ends up worse than before. That's what this generation actin' like."
12.46: While Jesus was still talkin' to the crowd, His mama and brothers showed up outside, tryna get a word with Him.
12.47: Somebody said, "Hey Jesus—Your mama and brothers outside waitin' to talk to You."
12.48: Jesus said, "Who really My mama? Who really My brothers?"
12.49: He pointed to His disciples and said, "Here they go—this My family.
12.50: Anybody who doin' the will of My Father in heaven? That's My brother, sister, and mama."

13.1: That same day, Jesus left the house and went to go sit by the sea.
13.2: A huge crowd pulled up, so He got in a boat and sat down, while everybody else stood on the shore.
13.3: He started teachin' through stories and said, "Look, a farmer went out to plant some seeds.
13.4: Some fell on the road, and birds came and snatched 'em up.
13.5: Some fell on rocky ground where there wasn't much dirt. They grew quick but had no depth.
13.6: The sun came up, scorched 'em, and since they had no roots, they dried up.
13.7: Some landed in thorny patches—the thorns grew up and choked 'em.
13.8: But some fell on good soil and produced a harvest—some a hundred times, some sixty, some thirty.
13.9: If you got ears, listen up!"
13.10: His disciples came and asked, "Why You always talkin' to them in parables?"
13.11: He said, "Because y'all been given access to the mysteries of the kingdom—but they ain't.
13.12: If you got it, you gon' get more. If you don't, even what you got gon' get snatched.
13.13: I speak in parables 'cause they lookin' but ain't really seein', hearin' but don't understand.
13.14: Isaiah already said it would be like this:
13.15: 'These folks' hearts done got hard. Their ears barely work. Their eyes stay closed—'cause if they really saw, heard, and understood, they'd turn around and get healed.'
13.16: But y'all? Y'all blessed. Your eyes see. Your ears hear.
13.17: Truth is, a whole lotta prophets and righteous folks wanted to see what y'all see—and they ain't get to. They wanted to hear this, but they never did."
13.19: Some folks hear the word about the kingdom but don't understand it. Then the enemy slides in and snatches it away—that's the seed on the road.
13.20: The rocky ground? That's folks who hear the word and get hype real quick—
13.21: But they got no root. So the second life gets hard or folks start hatin' on them for believin'? They fall off.
13.22: Seed in the thorns? That's folks who hear it, but stressin' over life and chasin' money chokes the word—it don't go nowhere.
13.23: But seed on good soil? That's folks who hear the word, understand it, and actually produce fruit—some thirty, some sixty, some a hundredfold."
13.24: "God's kingdom is like a man who planted good seed in his field.
13.25: But while everybody was sleep, his enemy came and planted weeds among the wheat.
13.26: When stuff started growin', the weeds popped up too.
13.27: The workers asked the owner, 'Didn't you plant good seed? Why we got weeds?'
13.28: He said, 'An enemy did this.' They asked, 'You want us to pull 'em up?'
13.29: He said, 'Nah, you might mess up the wheat too.
13.30: Let both grow together. Then at harvest, we'll separate—burn the weeds and store the wheat in the barn.'"
13.31: "The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed—a tiny thing someone plants in a field.
13.32: But when it grows, it becomes the biggest plant out there—so big birds post up in its branches."
13.33: "The kingdom is like yeast a woman mixes into flour. It don't look like much at first, but soon the whole batch rises."
13.34: Jesus told the crowd all this in parables. He didn't speak to them without stories.
13.35: That fulfilled what the prophet said: "I'll open My mouth in parables. I'll tell hidden things from the beginning of time."
13.36: Then Jesus dipped with His disciples, and they asked, "Break down that weeds parable."
13.37: He said, "The one plantin' good seed is the Son of Man.
13.38: The field is the world. Good seed? That's the kingdom's people. Weeds? That's the devil's crew.
13.39: The enemy who planted the weeds is Satan. The harvest? That's the end of time. And the workers are angels.
13.40: Just like weeds get gathered and burned, that's how it's gon' go down at the end.
13.41: The Son of Man gon' send angels to gather up every evil thing and everybody livin' lawless.
13.42: They'll get thrown in the fire—there's gon' be weepin' and teeth-grindin'.
13.43: But the righteous? They gon' shine bright like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. If you got ears, listen up!"
13.44: "The kingdom is like a treasure hid in a field. A man finds it, hides it again, and then sells everything he got to buy that field.
13.45: The kingdom is like a merchant huntin' for fine pearls.
13.46: When he finds that one priceless pearl, he sells all he has to buy it.
13.47: It's also like a big fishin' net thrown into the sea, catchin' all kinds of fish.
13.48: When it's full, they pull it up, sort the good into containers, and toss the bad.
13.49: That's how it's gon' be at the end—angels separatin' the wicked from the righteous,
13.50: And tossin' the wicked into the fire. More weepin'. More teeth-grindin'."
13.51: Jesus asked, "Y'all understand all this?" They said, "Yeah, Lord."
13.52: He said, "Then every teacher trained in the kingdom is like a homeowner who brings out treasures—some old, some new."
13.53: When Jesus finished all these parables, He left.
13.54: He went back to His hometown and taught in their synagogue. Folks were shocked and said, "Where He get this wisdom and power from?
13.55: Ain't this the carpenter's son? Ain't Mary His mama? Ain't His brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
13.56: And His sisters? They all live around here. Where He get all this from?"
13.57: They were offended by Him. But Jesus said, "A prophet ain't honored in his own hood."
13.58: And He didn't do many miracles there—'cause they ain't believe.

14.1: Around that time, Herod the ruler heard all the stuff Jesus was doin'.
14.2: He told his people, "That's John the Baptist! He back from the dead, that's why He got all this power!"
14.3: See, Herod had arrested John, tied him up, and threw him in jail 'cause of Herodias—his brother Philip's wife.
14.4: John had called him out, sayin', "You ain't got no business takin' her as your wife."
14.5: Herod wanted to kill John, but he was scared of the crowd—they saw John as a real prophet.
14.6: But on Herod's birthday, Herodias' daughter came through dancin', and it had Herod wide open.
14.7: He made a promise in front of everybody—said she could ask for whatever she wanted.
14.8: Her mama told her what to say, so the girl said, "I want John the Baptist's head on a platter."
14.9: Herod didn't wanna do it, but he ain't wanna look soft in front of his guests. So he gave the order.
14.10: They went and beheaded John in jail.
14.11: His head got brought out on a platter and handed to the girl, and she gave it to her mama.
14.12: John's disciples came, took his body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus what happened.
14.13: When Jesus heard the news, He dipped out by boat to a quiet place by Himself. But the crowd wasn't tryna let Him go—they walked there on foot from all over.
14.14: When Jesus stepped out and saw the big crowd, His heart broke for them. So He started healing their sick.
14.15: By the time it got late, the disciples were like, "Jesus, we in the middle of nowhere. Send these folks to town to get some food."
14.16: But Jesus said, "They ain't gotta go. Y'all feed 'em."
14.17: They said, "All we got is five loaves and two fish."
14.19: He had the crowd sit down on the grass. Then He took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to the disciples. They passed it out to the people.
14.20: Everybody ate and got full. And when it was over, they picked up 12 baskets of leftovers.
14.21: That day, Jesus fed five thousand men—not even counting all the women and kids.
14.22: Right after that, Jesus told the disciples to hop in the boat and go ahead to the other side while He sent the crowd home.
14.23: After the crowd left, Jesus went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. By the time it got dark, He was still up there alone.
14.24: Meanwhile, the boat was way out on the water, gettin' tossed by the waves 'cause the wind was wild.
14.25: Around 3 to 6 a.m., Jesus came walkin' on the water toward them.
14.26: When the disciples saw Him, they freaked out like, "It's a ghost!" and started screamin'.
14.27: But Jesus said, "Calm down, y'all. It's Me—don't be scared."
14.28: Peter said, "Lord, if it's really You, tell me to come to You on the water."
14.29: Jesus said, "Come on." So Peter hopped out the boat and started walkin' on water toward Jesus.
14.30: But when he saw how crazy the wind was, he got shook and started sinkin'. He yelled, "Lord, save me!"
14.31: Jesus grabbed him immediately and said, "You had such little faith. Why'd you doubt?"
14.32: As soon as they got back in the boat, the wind stopped.
14.33: Everybody in the boat bowed down and said, "You really are the Son of God."
14.34: When they got to the other side, they landed in Gennesaret.
14.35: Folks there recognized Jesus quick. They went and told everybody around, and soon sick folks were comin' from everywhere.
14.36: They begged Him, "Let us just touch the edge of Your clothes." And everybody who touched Him got healed completely.

15.1: Some religious folks—Pharisees and scribes straight outta Jerusalem—pulled up on Jesus and said,
15.2: "Why your crew don't follow tradition? They eatin' without washin' their hands!"
15.3: Jesus said, "Why y'all so pressed about tradition when you break God's commandments over it?
15.4: God said, 'Respect your mama and daddy,' and 'If you curse your folks, you supposed to be dealt with.'
15.5: But y'all say, 'If I give my money to God instead of my parents, I'm good.'
15.6: So now you lettin' people skip honorin' their parents for the sake of y'all's tradition. That means God's word ain't even hittin' no more 'cause of y'all.
15.7: Hypocrites! Isaiah was talkin' 'bout y'all when he said:
15.8: 'These people talk good with they mouth, But their hearts? Way far from Me.
15.9: They worship Me for nothin', Teachin' man-made rules like they from God.'"
15.10: Then Jesus turned to the crowd and said, "Listen and understand this—
15.11: It ain't what go in your mouth that makes you dirty. It's what comes out your mouth that shows what's really inside."
15.12: The disciples came to Him like, "Jesus… You know You offended the Pharisees with that, right?"
15.13: Jesus said, "Any plant My Father didn't plant? It's gettin' pulled up.
15.14: Leave them alone. They blind, leadin' blind. Both gon' end up in a ditch."
15.15: Peter said, "Lord, can You break that down for us?"
15.16: Jesus said, "Y'all still don't get it?
15.17: Food goes in, passes through the body—it's temporary.
15.18: But the stuff that comes out your mouth? That's from the heart—and that's what makes you messed up.
15.19: 'Cause out the heart come evil thoughts, murder, cheating, sex outside of God's will, theft, lies, and blasphemy.
15.20: That's what defiles you. Eating with unwashed hands ain't the problem."
15.21: Jesus left and went up to Tyre and Sidon.
15.22: A Canaanite woman from the area ran up cryin', "Lord, Son of David! Please help! My daughter possessed by a demon real bad."
15.23: Jesus ain't say a word. His disciples were like, "Can You send her away? She's loud and beggin' nonstop."
15.24: Jesus said, "I was sent for the lost sheep of Israel—My people."
15.25: But she came closer, bowed down, and said, "Lord, help me."
15.26: Jesus said, "It ain't right to take the kids' bread and toss it to the dogs."
15.27: She said, "True… but even the dogs eat the crumbs from the table."
15.28: Jesus lit up and said, "Woman, your faith is somethin' else! It's done—just like you asked." And her daughter got healed right then.
15.29: Jesus moved along by the Sea of Galilee, went up on a mountain, and sat down.
15.30: Big crowds came, bringin' the lame, blind, mute, disabled, and all kinds of sick folks. They dropped them at Jesus' feet—and He healed them.
15.31: People couldn't believe it. Mute folks speakin'. Crippled folks whole again. Lame folks walkin'. Blind folks seein'. And they gave all the glory to the God of Israel.
15.32: Jesus told His disciples, "I'm feelin' for this crowd. They've been with Me three days and they got nothin' left to eat. I can't send them off hungry—they might pass out on the way."
15.33: The disciples said, "Jesus… where we supposed to get enough food for all these folks out here in the middle of nowhere?"
15.34: Jesus said, "How many loaves we got?" They said, "Seven, and a few little fish."
15.35: Jesus told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
15.36: He took the loaves and fish, gave thanks, broke 'em, and handed 'em to His disciples to pass out.
15.37: Everybody ate and got full. Then they picked up seven big baskets of leftovers.
15.38: That day He fed four thousand men—not even countin' all the women and kids.
15.39: After that, Jesus told the crowd to head out. Then He got in a boat and went to the region of Magdala.

16.1: The Pharisees and Sadducees rolled up on Jesus, tryna test Him. They said, "Show us somethin' from heaven—give us a sign."
16.2: Jesus said, "Y'all real quick to call the weather, right? In the evening you say, 'Sky red, it's gon' be nice tomorrow.'
16.3: And in the morning, 'Sky red and cloudy—rain's comin.' Y'all can read the sky, but can't even read the signs of the times.
16.4: Y'all a wicked, unfaithful generation. Always lookin' for signs. The only sign you gon' get is the sign of Jonah." And He dipped on 'em.
16.5: Later on, when they got to the other side, the disciples realized—they forgot to bring bread.
16.6: Jesus told them, "Watch out. Be careful of the leaven from the Pharisees and Sadducees."
16.7: They started whisperin', "He sayin' that 'cause we ain't got no bread."
16.8: Jesus knew what they was thinkin' and said, "Y'all got little faith. Why y'all stressin' about bread?
16.9: Don't y'all remember when I fed five thousand with five loaves? How many baskets y'all picked up?
16.10: Or the four thousand with seven loaves? How many baskets then?
16.11: So how y'all still think I'm talkin' 'bout actual bread? I'm sayin' be careful of the teaching from them Pharisees and Sadducees."
16.12: Then they got it—He wasn't talkin' food. He was talkin' 'bout that fake doctrine they be spreadin'.
16.13: When Jesus got to Caesarea Philippi, He asked His crew, "Who folks say I am?"
16.14: They said, "Some think You John the Baptist, some Elijah, some Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
16.15: He said, "Aight, but who you say I am?"
16.16: Peter spoke up: "You the Christ. The Son of the livin' God."
16.17: Jesus said, "Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! Ain't no human tell you that—My Father in heaven dropped that revelation.
16.18: And I'm tellin' you, you Peter, and on this rock I'ma build My Church. Hell itself ain't strong enough to stop it.
16.19: I'ma give you the keys to the kingdom. Whatever you lock down on earth gon' be locked in heaven. Whatever you open up on earth gon' be opened in heaven."
16.20: Then He told them, "Don't tell nobody I'm the Christ. Not yet."
16.21: From that point on, Jesus started lettin' them know: "I gotta go to Jerusalem. I'm gon' suffer under the elders, priests, and scribes. They gon' kill Me. But on the third day? I'm risin' up."
16.22: Peter pulled Him aside like, "Lord nah! That can't happen to You!"
16.23: Jesus turned to Peter like, "Get behind Me, Satan! You in My way. You thinkin' like a man—not with God's mindset."
16.24: Then Jesus told the crew, "If you wanna roll with Me, deny yourself. Carry your cross and follow Me.
16.25: Try to save your life? You gon' lose it. But lose it for Me? That's how you find real life.
16.26: What good is gainin' the whole world if you lose your soul in the process? What could you even trade for your soul?
16.27: The Son of Man gon' come through in glory, rollin' with the angels. And He gon' pay everybody back based on what they done.
16.28: Let Me tell you this—some of y'all standin' here right now won't die before you see the Son of Man comin' into His Kingdom."

17.1: Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John (his brother), and they went up on a high mountain—just the four of them.
17.2: While they was up there, Jesus changed right in front of them—His face started shinin' like the sun, and His clothes was bright white like light itself.
17.3: Then outta nowhere, Moses and Elijah showed up, choppin' it up with Jesus.
17.4: Peter jumped in, "Lord, this is perfect! If You want, I'll build three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
17.5: But while Peter was still talkin', a bright cloud came over them, and a voice boomed from it: "This My Son, the One I love. I'm pleased with Him. Listen to Him!"
17.6: When the disciples heard that, they hit the ground face-first—they was shook.
17.7: But Jesus walked over, touched 'em and said, "Y'all get up. Don't be scared."
17.8: They looked up, and Moses and Elijah was gone—only Jesus was still there.
17.9: As they came down the mountain, Jesus said, "Don't tell nobody what you saw 'til after I rise from the dead."
17.10: The disciples asked Him, "Why do the scribes say Elijah gotta come first?"
17.11: Jesus said, "They right—Elijah is supposed to come and get things back in order.
17.12: But I'm tellin' y'all, Elijah already came, and folks ain't even recognize him. They did him dirty. Same thing gon' happen to the Son of Man."
17.13: Then the disciples realized He was talkin' about John the Baptist.
17.14: When they came back down to the crowd, a man came kneelin' and beggin':
17.15: "Lord, please help my son. He got seizures real bad. Sometimes he fall into fire or water.
17.16: I tried bringin' him to Your disciples, but they couldn't heal him."
17.17: Jesus said, "This generation got no faith and is twisted up… How long I gotta deal with y'all? Bring the boy here."
17.18: Jesus spoke to the demon, rebuked it, and it came out. The boy was healed right then.
17.19: Later, the disciples asked Him in private, "Why couldn't we cast it out?"
17.20: Jesus said, "Because y'all didn't believe enough. I'm tellin' you—for real—for real, if you got faith the size of a mustard seed, you could tell a mountain to move and it would. Nothin' would be impossible.
17.21: But this type of demon? It don't leave unless you fast and pray."
17.22: While they was stayin' in Galilee, Jesus told them, "The Son of Man bout to be handed over.
17.23: They gon' kill Me, but on the third day, I'm gettin' up." The disciples were heartbroken.
17.24: When they got to Capernaum, the temple tax collectors pulled up on Peter like, "Yo, don't your Teacher pay the tax?"
17.25: Peter said, "Yeah, He do." But when he walked into the house, Jesus already knew what was up. He asked, "Let me ask you this, Simon—do kings charge their own sons taxes, or just other people?"
17.26: Peter said, "Other folks." Jesus said, "Exactly. So technically, the sons don't gotta pay.
17.27: But to keep the peace, go fishin'. First fish you catch? Open its mouth—you gon' find some money in there. Take that and pay the tax for both of us."

18.1: The disciples came up like, "Jesus, who really the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
18.2: Jesus pulled a little kid over and sat them right in the middle of the group.
18.3: He said, "For real, unless y'all change and become like this lil one, you ain't even gettin' in the kingdom.
18.4: Whoever humble themself like this child—that's who the greatest out here.
18.5: And anybody who welcomes a child like this in My name? You welcoming Me too."
18.6: "If you cause one of these lil ones who believe in Me to mess up? You'd be better off with a stone tied to your neck and tossed in the ocean.
18.7: This world full of temptation and traps—yeah, that's gonna happen. But woe to the one bringin' it.
18.8: If your hand or your foot makin' you sin, cut it off. It's better to roll into eternal life with one arm or leg than to be whole and thrown in the fire.
18.9: Same with your eye—if it's trippin', pluck it out. One eye in heaven beat two in hell."
18.10: "Don't look down on these little ones. I'm tellin' you—they got angels in heaven who stay facin' My Father.
18.11: I came to save the ones who got lost.
18.12: Imagine you got 100 sheep, and one wander off. Ain't you gon' leave the 99 and go lookin' for that one?
18.13: And when you find it? You rejoicin' over that one more than the 99 that stayed put.
18.14: That's how your Father in heaven is—He don't want none of these lil ones to get lost."
18.15: "If your brother or sister wrong you, go talk to them one-on-one. If they listen, boom—you got your sibling back.
18.16: If they don't, bring one or two folks with you, so the truth got witnesses.
18.17: If they still ain't listenin', bring it to the whole church. And if they won't hear the church? Treat 'em like an outsider or tax man.
18.18: I'm sayin' to y'all—whatever y'all lock down on earth is locked in heaven, and whatever y'all free on earth is free in heaven.
18.19: If two of y'all agree on somethin' and ask My Father? He gon' do it.
18.20: 'Cause when two or three gather in My name? I'm right there in the middle."
18.21: Peter said, "Lord, how many times I gotta forgive my brother when he mess up? Seven times?"
18.22: Jesus said, "Nah, not seven—seventy times seven. Keep forgivin'.
18.23: The kingdom of heaven is like a king settlin' accounts.
18.24: One servant owed him 10,000 bags of silver. That man couldn't pay,
18.25: so the king said, 'Sell him, his wife, kids—everything—so I can get some of it back.'
18.26: The servant dropped to his knees: 'Please, be patient! I'll pay it back!'
18.27: The king had compassion, let him go, and canceled the whole debt.
18.28: But that same servant turned around, found a dude who owed him just 100 coins, and choked him: 'Run me my money!'
18.29: The other servant begged, 'Please, give me some time.'
18.30: But he said no and had him locked up 'til he paid.
18.31: When the other workers saw it, they were hurt, and told the king what happened.
18.32: The king called him back like, 'You evil servant! I forgave you that big debt 'cause you begged me.
18.33: Shouldn't you have showed mercy to your coworker like I did you?'
18.34: Then the king got heated, and handed him over to be punished until he paid it all.
18.35: And My Father in heaven gon' do the same to y'all, if you don't forgive your brother or sister from the heart."

19.1: After Jesus finished teachin', He left Galilee and headed down to Judea, across the Jordan.
19.2: Big crowds followed Him, and He healed the sick like He always do.
19.3: Some Pharisees pulled up, tryin' to trap Him: "So Jesus, is it cool for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?"
19.4: Jesus said, "Y'all don't read Scripture? God made them male and female from jump.
19.5: And He said, 'A man gon' leave his parents and be joined to his wife. The two become one body.'
19.6: So they ain't two no more—they one. What God put together, can't no man tear apart."
19.7: They said, "Then why Moses say we could hand out divorce papers and let her go?"
19.8: Jesus replied, "That was Moses makin' space 'cause y'all hearts was hard. But that ain't how it was supposed to be from the beginning.
19.9: I'm tellin' you now—anybody who divorces his wife except for cheatin' and marries somebody else, that's adultery. Same if you marry a woman who's been divorced like that."
19.10: The disciples was like, "Whew. If that's how marriage is, maybe we just shouldn't marry at all."
19.11: Jesus said, "That ain't for everybody to handle. Only folks who been graced to live like that.
19.12: Some people born without the ability, some been made that way by others, and some chose it for the Kingdom. If you can handle it, handle it."
19.13: Then some folks brought their lil kids to Jesus so He could bless and pray over them. But the disciples tried to shut it down.
19.14: Jesus said, "Uh uh. Let the kids come. Don't stop 'em. The Kingdom belongs to people like this."
19.15: Then He laid hands on the kids and kept it movin'.
19.16: A young man ran up: "Good Teacher, what I gotta do to get eternal life?"
19.17: Jesus said, "Why you callin' Me good? Only God is truly good. But if you tryna live forever, keep the commandments."
19.18: The young man said, "Which ones?" Jesus replied, "Don't kill. Don't cheat. Don't steal. Don't lie.
19.19: Respect your parents. Love your neighbor like you love yourself."
19.20: The guy said, "I've done all that since I was young. What am I still missin'?"
19.21: Jesus said, "If you wanna be whole for real, go sell everything you got and give the money to the poor. Then come follow Me—you'll have treasure in heaven."
19.22: But the man walked away sad, 'cause he had a lot of money and didn't wanna let it go.
19.23: Jesus looked at His crew and said, "I'm tellin' y'all straight up—it's hard for rich folks to make it into the Kingdom.
19.24: Matter fact, it's easier for a camel to squeeze through a needle's eye than for a rich person to enter God's Kingdom."
19.25: The disciples looked around like, "Well dang, who can be saved then?"
19.26: Jesus looked right at them: "With people? Impossible. But with God? All things possible."
19.27: Peter said, "Lord, we left everything to follow You. So what's gon' be ours?"
19.28: Jesus said, "Y'all who been ridin' with Me—when the new world come and I'm sittin' on My throne, y'all gon' sit on thrones too, judgin' the twelve tribes of Israel.
19.29: And anybody who left their house, siblings, parents, spouse, kids, or land for Me? They gon' get it back a hundred times over and get eternal life.
19.30: But just know—folks who seem first now? They gon' be last. And the ones y'all overlook now? They gon' be first."

20.1: Jesus said, "The Kingdom of Heaven like this man who owned some land. Dude woke up early, went out lookin' for folks to work his vineyard.
20.2: He found some workers, agreed to pay 'em a denarius for the day, and sent 'em out to the field.
20.3: Around 9AM, he went back to the marketplace and saw some folks just chillin', not doin' nothin'.
20.4: He said, 'Aight, y'all go work too. I'ma pay what's fair.' So they dipped.
20.5: He came back around noon, and again around 3PM, and told more folks the same thing.
20.6: Then around 5PM—real late in the day—he pulled up again. Saw some folks still standin' around like, "Ain't nobody picked us yet."
20.7: He said, 'Go ahead and work in the vineyard too. I got you.'
20.8: Come clock-out time, the boss said to his manager, 'Call everybody up. Pay the ones who started last first.'
20.9: So the folks who only worked one hour stepped up—and boom—they each got a whole denarius.
20.10: When the ones who started early saw that, they thought they'd get more. But nah, they got the same amount.
20.12: 'Hold up! These last folks only worked an hour, and you gave them what we got? We been out here in the heat all day!'
20.13: But the boss told one of them, 'Fam, I ain't cheat you. Didn't we agree on a denarius?
20.14: Take your money and go. I chose to give the last man the same as you.
20.15: Ain't it my money? Can't I do what I want with it? Or you mad 'cause I'm generous?'
20.16: That's why I'm tellin' y'all—the last gon' be first, and the first gon' be last. Plenty folks get the call, but not everybody makes the cut."
20.17: As they headed toward Jerusalem, Jesus pulled the twelve aside for a real talk.
20.18: He said, "Look—we goin' up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man (that's Me) gon' get betrayed to the religious leaders. They gon' sentence Me to death,
20.19: and hand Me over to the Romans. They gon' mock Me, beat Me, and crucify Me. But on the third day—I'm gettin' up."
20.20: Then the mama of James and John (Zebedee's sons) pulled up on Jesus with her boys, kneelin' and tryin' to put in a request.
20.21: Jesus asked, "What you want?" She said, "Promise me my sons can sit right beside You in Your kingdom—one on the left, one on the right."
20.22: Jesus said, "You don't even know what you askin'. Can y'all drink the cup I'm about to drink? Can you go through what I'm 'bout to go through?" They said, "Yeah, we got it."
20.23: Jesus said, "Oh, you will drink from my cup, but those seats? That ain't up to Me. That's for the ones God already got lined up."
20.24: The other ten disciples heard about this and got heated.
20.25: So Jesus sat 'em all down and said, "Look—out there, folks in power love to boss people around. That ain't how we roll.
20.26: If you wanna be great in this Kingdom? Serve.
20.27: Wanna be first? Be the one who waits on everybody.
20.28: Even I, the Son of Man, didn't come to be served—I came to serve and to give My life to save many."
20.29: As they left Jericho, a big crowd followed Jesus.
20.30: Two blind men were sittin' by the road, and when they heard Jesus was passin' by, they shouted, "Son of David! Have mercy on us!"
20.31: The crowd tried to shut them up, but they yelled even louder, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
20.32: Jesus stopped in His tracks, called 'em over, and asked, "What y'all want Me to do for you?"
20.33: They said, "Lord, we tryna see again."
20.34: Jesus felt it in His heart, touched their eyes, and boom—they could see. And they ain't hesitate—they got up and followed Him.

21.1: When Jesus and the crew got close to Jerusalem, near Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples ahead.
21.2: He told them, "Go into the village in front of y'all. Right when you get there, you gon' see a donkey tied up and a young colt with her. Untie them and bring them to Me.
21.3: If anybody say anything to y'all, just say, 'The Lord need them,' and they gon' let you take them."
21.4: This whole thing went down so what the prophet said would come true:
21.5: "Tell Zion's daughter, 'Look, your King comin' to you. He ain't pullin' up flashy—He ridin' humble on a donkey, a young one.'"
21.6: So the disciples went and did just like Jesus told them.
21.7: They brought the donkey and the colt, laid their coats on 'em, and Jesus got up on top of them.
21.8: A big crowd started layin' they coats on the road, and others were cuttin' down branches from trees and puttin' 'em down too.
21.9: The folks in front and behind Jesus was shoutin' out, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Bless the One who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
21.10: When He rolled into Jerusalem, the whole city got shook. Folks was like, "Who is this?"
21.11: And the crowd said, "That's Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee."
21.12: Jesus went straight into the temple and started clearing it out—He flipped over the tables of the money folks and the seats of the bird-sellers.
21.13: He said, "Scripture say, 'My house shall be a house of prayer,' but y'all done turned it into a trap house for thieves."
21.14: Then the blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them right there.
21.15: But the religious leaders—the priests and scribes—saw all the dope things He was doing, and heard the kids yellin', "Hosanna to the Son of David!" and they got tight about it.
21.16: They said to Jesus, "You hear what these kids sayin'?" Jesus said, "Yeah. Ain't y'all ever read, 'Outta the mouth of babies and little ones comes real praise'?"
21.17: After that, He left and went to Bethany and spent the night there.
21.18: The next morning, Jesus was hungry on the way back to the city.
21.19: He saw a fig tree on the side of the road and walked up to it, but it ain't have nothin' but leaves. So He said, "You ain't gon' grow no fruit ever again." And boom—the tree dried up just like that.
21.20: The disciples saw it happen and was like, "Whoa! How that tree die so fast?"
21.21: Jesus said, "If y'all got faith and don't doubt, y'all can do this too—and even tell a mountain, 'Move over there,' and it'll do it.
21.22: Whatever you ask in prayer, believe you gon' get it, and it'll come."
21.23: Jesus came back to the temple, and while He was teaching, the top priests and elders rolled up on Him and said, "Who told you you could do all this? Who gave you that kind of authority?"
21.24: Jesus said, "Lemme ask y'all one thing first. If y'all answer me, then I'll tell you who gave Me authority.
21.25: John's baptism—did it come from heaven or from people?" They huddled up and whispered, "If we say heaven, He gon' ask why we ain't believe John.
21.26: But if we say it was just from people, the crowd might turn on us—they all think John was a real prophet."
21.27: So they told Jesus, "We don't know." And Jesus said, "Well then, I ain't tellin' y'all either."
21.28: "Now y'all tell Me this. A man had two sons. He went to the first one and said, 'Son, go work in the vineyard today.'
21.29: The son said, 'Nah, I ain't goin.' But later he felt bad and went anyway.
21.30: Then the man told his second son the same thing, and he said, 'Yes sir, I'm on it,' but he ain't go.
21.31: Which one actually did what his daddy wanted?" They said, "The first." Jesus replied, "Exactly. That's why tax collectors and prostitutes gettin' into God's kingdom before y'all.
21.32: John came through showin' y'all the righteous way, and y'all ain't believe him. But the tax men and the women in the streets did. And even when y'all saw that, you ain't change your minds and believe."
21.33: "Here's another one for y'all. A landowner planted a vineyard. He put a fence around it, dug a winepress, built a tower, and rented it out to some farmers. Then he dipped out to another place.
21.34: When harvest time came, he sent his workers to collect his part of the crop.
21.35: But the renters beat one, killed another, and stoned the third.
21.36: So the landowner sent more workers—more than the first time—and they did the same thing to them.
21.37: Finally, he sent his own son, thinking, 'They gon' respect my boy.'
21.38: But when they saw the son, they said, 'This the heir! Let's kill him and get everything for ourselves.'
21.39: So they grabbed him, threw him out the vineyard, and murdered him."
21.40: "Now when the owner of the vineyard shows up, what y'all think he gon' do?"
21.41: They said, "He gon' destroy them dudes for sure, and lease the vineyard to others who gon' give him his share at harvest."
21.42: Jesus said, "Y'all ever read the Scriptures? 'The stone the builders rejected Became the main cornerstone. That was God's doing, And it's mind-blowing to see.'"
21.43: "That's why I'm telling y'all—the kingdom of God gon' be taken from you and handed over to folks who gon' actually do something with it.
21.44: And anybody who stumbles over that stone gon' get broken. And if it falls on somebody—it's gon' crush them completely."
21.45: When the priests and Pharisees heard this story, they knew He was talkin' about them.
21.46: They wanted to grab Him right then—but they were scared of the crowd, 'cause everybody thought Jesus was a real prophet.

22.1: Jesus kept talkin' in parables and said,
22.2: "The kingdom of heaven like a king who threw a big wedding for his son.
22.3: He sent his people to go get the invited guests, but they ain't wanna come.
22.4: So he sent more folks, sayin', 'Tell the ones invited, "Dinner ready! I done cooked the ox and the best meat. Everything set—come on to the wedding!"'
22.5: But they blew it off. One went to work on his farm, another went to handle his business.
22.6: The rest straight up jumped the messengers, disrespected them, and killed them.
22.7: The king heard about it and got heated. He sent his army, got rid of them murderers, and set their city on fire.
22.8: Then he told his people, 'The wedding ready, but the invited ones ain't worthy.
22.9: So go out into the streets and bring in everybody you see.'
22.10: So the servants went out, grabbed whoever they could find—good or bad—and the wedding hall got packed.
22.11: But when the king came in to check the guests, he spotted one dude not dressed for the occasion.
22.12: He said, 'Bruh, how you get in here with no wedding clothes?' Dude ain't say nothin'.
22.13: So the king told the servants, 'Tie him up and throw him into the dark, where folk cry and grind their teeth.'
22.14: A lotta folks get called, but only a few get picked."
22.15: Then the Pharisees linked up to try and trip Jesus up with His own words.
22.16: They sent their people, along with some of Herod's crew, and said, "Teacher, we know You keep it real and speak truth from God. You ain't pressed about folks' opinions either.
22.17: So tell us, is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or nah?"
22.18: But Jesus peeped their game and said, "Why y'all playin' with Me, you hypocrites?
22.19: Show Me the coin used for taxes."
22.20: He said, "Whose face and name on this?"
22.22: Jesus said, "Then give Caesar what's his—and give God what's God's."
22.23: That same day, some Sadducees—who don't believe in the resurrection—came with a question.
22.24: "Teacher," they said, "Moses said if a man dies with no kids, his brother gotta marry the widow and raise up kids for him.
22.25: So there was seven brothers. First one married, died with no kids, left his wife to his brother.
22.26: Same with the second, and the third, all the way to the seventh.
22.28: So in the resurrection, whose wife she gonna be, since all seven had her?"
22.29: Jesus said, "Y'all wrong 'cause you don't know Scripture or God's power.
22.30: In the resurrection, folks don't marry—they like the angels in heaven.
22.31: And as for the dead bein' raised—ain't you read what God said?
22.32: 'I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' He ain't God of the dead—He the God of the living."
22.33: The crowd was blown away by that answer.
22.34: When the Pharisees heard Jesus had shut the Sadducees down, they huddled up.
22.35: One of them—a lawyer—tried to test Jesus with a question.
22.36: "Teacher, which commandment the biggest in the law?"
22.37: Jesus said, "'Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind.'
22.38: That's the first and biggest one.
22.39: But the second one right there with it: 'Love your neighbor like you love yourself.'
22.40: Everything in the Law and the Prophets hang on these two."
22.41: While the Pharisees were still hangin' around, Jesus hit them with a question.
22.42: "What y'all think about the Christ—whose Son is He?"
22.43: He said, "Then how come David, speakin' by the Spirit, calls Him 'Lord'? He said:
22.44: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand, Till I make Your enemies Your footstool."'
22.45: So if David call Him 'Lord,' how's He his son?"
