22.46: Nobody had a comeback. From that day on, they ain't dare ask Jesus no more questions.

23.1: Then Jesus started speakin' to the crowd and His disciples.
23.2: He said, "The scribes and Pharisees sittin' up in Moses' seat like they runnin' things.
23.3: So yeah, do what they say when it line up with the Word—but don't be actin' like them, 'cause they be talkin' big but don't live none of it.
23.4: They pile heavy rules on folks' backs, stuff hard to carry, but they ain't liftin' a finger to help.
23.5: Everything they do is just for show. They rockin' extra big scripture boxes on they clothes and stretchin' the hems like that make 'em holy.
23.6: They love the VIP seats at parties and front-row pews at church.
23.7: They live for attention in the streets and love when folks call 'em 'Rabbi.'
23.8: But don't let nobody call you 'Rabbi,' 'cause y'all got one real Teacher—the Messiah—and all y'all fam.
23.9: Don't be callin' folks 'Father' down here, 'cause you got one true Father in heaven.
23.10: And don't be tryin' to flex titles like 'Teacher'—you got one, and that's Christ.
23.11: The greatest one in the crew? That's the one servin' everybody else.
23.12: If you stay humble, you'll get lifted. But if you always tryna lift yourself up, you gon' get brought down."
23.13: "Woe to y'all fake scribes and Pharisees—straight hypocrites! You blockin' folks from gettin' to the kingdom. You ain't goin' in, and you stoppin' others from goin' in too.
23.14: Woe to y'all who scam widows outta they homes and then try to cover it with long, fake prayers. Y'all gon' catch a heavier judgment.
23.15: Woe again! Y'all cross land and sea just to get one convert, and when you finally do, you turn 'em into twice the devil you are.
23.16: Woe to y'all blind guides, talkin' 'bout, 'If you swear by the temple, that don't count, but if you swear by the gold inside it, you locked in.'
23.17: Man, y'all foolish and blind! What's greater—the gold or the temple that made the gold holy?
23.18: Same thing with the altar—you say swearin' by the gift on it means somethin', but the altar itself don't?
23.19: Y'all wild. What's more important—the gift or the altar that makes it holy?
23.20: If you swear by the altar, you swear by everything on it.
23.21: Swear by the temple? That's swearin' by the One who live there.
23.22: Swear by heaven? You swearin' on God's throne—and on God, period."
23.23: "Woe to y'all again—tithin' on your herbs like mint, anise, and cumin, but forgettin' justice, mercy, and real faith. Y'all shoulda did all that, without forgettin' the important stuff.
23.24: Y'all blind guides, straining out a little gnat but swallowin' a whole camel.
23.25: Woe! Y'all clean the outside of the cup, but inside y'all full of greed and mess.
23.26: Blind Pharisee—clean the inside first, then the outside gon' follow.
23.27: Woe again! Y'all like painted tombs—lookin' good on the outside, but inside y'all full of bones and dead man vibes.
23.28: Y'all look righteous, but y'all hearts full of hypocrisy and sin."
23.29: "Woe again! Y'all build tombs for the prophets and dress 'em up like you honor 'em,
23.30: sayin', 'If we'd been around back then, we wouldn't have killed God's messengers.'
23.31: But by sayin' that, you confessin' y'all sons of the same folks who did kill 'em.
23.32: Go 'head then—fill up the cup of guilt your ancestors started.
23.33: Snakes! Offspring of vipers! How y'all think you gon' escape hell's judgment?
23.34: I'ma send prophets, wise folks, and teachers—and y'all gon' kill, crucify, and beat some of 'em down in church, chasin' them city to city.
23.35: Because of that, all the righteous blood ever spilled—starting from Abel all the way to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, who y'all killed in the temple—is comin' down on this generation.
23.36: I'm tellin' y'all now: all this gon' hit y'all soon."
23.37: "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem… killin' prophets and stonin' the ones sent to save you. I been tryna gather y'all like a mama hen with her chicks, but y'all wasn't havin' it.
23.38: Look at your house—left empty, abandoned.
23.39: I'm tellin' you now, you won't see Me again till you say, 'Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord.'"

24.1: Jesus walked out the temple, and His disciples was showin' off how fine the buildings looked.
24.2: But Jesus told 'em, "Y'all see all this? I'm tellin' you straight—ain't gon' be one stone left on top another. It's all gon' come crashin' down."
24.3: Later on, Jesus was chillin' on the Mount of Olives when the disciples came to Him on the low and asked, "So when all this gon' happen? What the sign that You comin' back and the world wrappin' up?"
24.4: Jesus said, "Look, don't let nobody play y'all.
24.5: Folks gon' come actin' like they Me, sayin' they the Christ, and gon' fool a lotta people.
24.6: You gon' hear 'bout wars and threats of wars. Don't panic though—this gotta happen, but that ain't the end yet.
24.7: Nations gon' beef with each other, kingdoms gon' clash. There gon' be famines, plagues, and earthquakes all over.
24.8: That's just the warm-up though—the start of the pain.
24.9: Then they gon' hand y'all over to be mistreated, even killed. Everybody gon' hate y'all just 'cause y'all reppin' Me.
24.10: Folks gon' fall off, betray each other, and turn cold with hate.
24.11: Fake prophets gon' rise up and fool folks.
24.12: And since everybody wildin' out and doin' dirt, love gon' grow cold.
24.13: But the one who hold on to the end? They gon' be saved.
24.14: And this good news about the Kingdom? It's gon' get preached all across the world for everybody to hear—and then the end gon' come."
24.15: "So when y'all see that nasty, messed-up thing Daniel talked about standin' in the holy spot—pay attention!
24.16: If you in Judea, run for the hills.
24.17: If you on the roof, don't go back in for nothin'.
24.18: If you in the field, don't go back to grab your coat.
24.19: Woe to the pregnant ladies and new mamas in those days!
24.20: Pray your escape ain't in winter or on the Sabbath.
24.21: 'Cause it's gon' be a time of trouble the world ain't never seen before—and won't ever see again.
24.22: If God ain't cut them days short, nobody would survive. But for His chosen ones' sake, He gon' cut it short.
24.23: So if somebody say, 'Look! The Christ over here!' or 'He over there!'—don't believe it.
24.24: Fake messiahs and prophets gon' show up, doin' wild signs and wonders, tryin' to fool even the real ones if they could.
24.25: I'm tellin' y'all now so y'all ain't caught slippin'.
24.26: So if they tell y'all, 'He out in the desert,' don't go. 'He hidin' in some secret spot,' don't believe that either.
24.27: 'Cause when I come back, it's gon' hit like lightning—boom, from the east to the west, real obvious.
24.28: Wherever there's a dead body, that's where the vultures gon' circle. Same with My return—it's gon' be clear."
24.29: "Right after that time of trouble, the sun gon' go dark, the moon won't shine, the stars gon' fall, and the heavens gon' shake.
24.30: Then everybody gon' see the sign of the Son of Man up in the sky. All the folks on earth gon' cry out when they see Me comin' on the clouds, powerful and shinin' in glory.
24.31: And I'ma send My angels with a loud trumpet blast, and they gon' gather My people from everywhere—north, south, east, west, all across heaven."
24.32: "Peep the fig tree: when you see it sproutin' leaves, you know summer close.
24.33: Same way, when you see all this goin' down, know that it's right at the door.
24.34: I'm tellin' you the truth—this generation ain't gon' pass till all this goes down.
24.35: Heaven and earth might pass away, but My words? They locked in forever."
24.36: "Nobody knows the day or hour—not the angels, not even Me—only the Father.
24.37: Just like in Noah's day, that's how it's gon' be when the Son of Man comes.
24.38: Folks was eatin', drinkin', gettin' married—livin' life—right up until Noah stepped in that ark.
24.39: They ain't know what hit 'em till the flood came and swept 'em all away. That's exactly how it's gon' be.
24.40: Two dudes gon' be in the field—one gone, the other stay.
24.41: Two women grindin' grain—one gone, the other left.
24.42: So stay woke! You don't know what time your Lord gon' pull up.
24.43: If the homeowner knew what time the thief was comin', he wouldn't have let his house get hit.
24.44: Be ready! The Son of Man gon' show up when you least expect it."
24.45: "So who's the wise and faithful servant the Master put in charge to look after the house and make sure folks eat on time?
24.46: Blessed is that one who still on they job when the Master shows up.
24.47: For real, He gon' put that one over all His stuff.
24.48: But say that servant wild out and say, 'My Master takin' too long,'
24.49: then starts beatin' the others and partyin' with the drunk crew—
24.50: That Master gon' show up on a day he ain't expectin' and at a time he ain't ready for.
24.51: He gon' cut him off, throw him with the hypocrites. And there? It's gon' be nothin' but cryin' and teeth-grindin'."

25.1: "The Kingdom of Heaven like this: ten young women grab they lamps and go out waitin' for the groom.
25.2: Five of 'em was wise. The other five? Straight foolish.
25.3: The silly ones brought they lamps but ain't bring no extra oil.
25.4: But the wise ones came ready—they had they lamps AND extra oil on deck.
25.5: The groom was takin' forever, so they all got sleepy and knocked out.
25.6: Around midnight, somebody yelled, 'Ayy! The groom comin'! Go meet him!'
25.7: All the girls jumped up and got they lamps lit.
25.8: The silly ones said to the wise, 'Let us get some of y'all oil—our lamps goin' out!'
25.9: The wise girls said, 'Uh uh. We ain't got enough for everybody. Go to the store and buy your own.'
25.10: While they was gone tryna buy oil, the groom came. The ones who were ready went in with him to the wedding, and the door got shut.
25.11: Later, the others came knockin', talkin' 'bout, 'Lord, Lord, open up!'
25.12: But he said, 'I'm tellin' you the truth—I don't even know y'all.'
25.13: So stay woke, 'cause you don't know the day or the hour when the Son of Man showin' up."
25.14: "It's like a man who was headin' outta town. He called his servants and handed over his money.
25.15: One got five bags of silver, another got two, and one got just one—each based on what he could handle. Then the boss dipped.
25.16: The one with five bags went to work and made five more.
25.17: The one with two doubled his up too.
25.18: But the one with one bag? He got scared, dug a hole, and hid the money.
25.19: A long time later, the boss came back and wanted his money checked.
25.20: The five-bag man said, 'Boss, you gave me five—I got five more!'
25.21: The boss said, 'Good job, my dude! You was faithful over a few things—I'ma put you over a lot. Come celebrate with me!'
25.22: The two-bag servant came up like, 'Boss, I flipped your two and got two more!'
25.23: The boss said, 'That's what I'm talkin' about! You did good too—come on in and enjoy this joy!'
25.24: Then the one with one bag stepped up. 'Boss, I know you tough. You take what you ain't plant and collect what you ain't scatter.
25.25: So I got scared and buried your money. Here go your one bag back.'
25.26: But the boss said, 'You lazy and wicked! If you knew how I move, you shoulda at least put my money in the bank so I could get interest.
25.28: Matter fact, give it to the one with ten bags.
25.29: Folks who handle they business get more. But folks who waste? Even what they got gon' get snatched.
25.30: And throw that sorry servant in the dark where folk cry and grind they teeth.'"
25.31: "When the Son of Man come in all His glory, with His angels, He gon' sit on His throne.
25.32: Everybody—every nation—gon' be in front of Him, and He gon' separate folks like a shepherd split sheep from goats.
25.33: Sheep on the right. Goats on the left.
25.34: Then the King gon' say to the folks on the right, 'Y'all blessed! Come on and get the Kingdom I been settin' up for you since day one.
25.35: I was hungry, and y'all fed Me. Thirsty, and y'all gave Me a drink. I was new around here, and y'all welcomed Me.
25.36: I ain't have clothes, and y'all covered Me. I was sick, and y'all checked on Me. I was locked up, and y'all visited Me.'
25.37: Then the righteous folks gon' say, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or locked up and take care of You?'
25.38: When did we see You a stranger and welcome You, or naked and give You clothes?
25.39: When did we see You sick or in prison and come to You?'
25.40: And the King gon' say, 'If you did it for the least of these—My people—you did it for Me.'
25.41: But then He gon' turn to the left and say, 'Get outta here, y'all cursed! Go to that eternal fire built for the devil and his crew!
25.42: I was hungry—you ain't feed Me. Thirsty—you ain't give Me nothin'.
25.43: I was a stranger—you ain't take Me in. Naked—you ain't cover Me. Sick and in jail—you ain't visit Me.'
25.44: And they gon' say, 'Lord, when did we see You like that and not help?'
25.45: He gon' say, 'If you ain't do it for the least of these, you ain't do it for Me.'
25.46: And them folks gon' go off into eternal punishment. But the righteous? Eternal life."

26.1: When Jesus finished sayin' all that, He told His crew,
26.2: "Y'all know Passover comin' in two days, right? That's when the Son of Man—Me—gon' be handed over and crucified."
26.3: Meanwhile, the high priests, teachers of the law, and elders met up at the high priest's spot—Caiaphas house—
26.4: tryin' to figure out how to set Jesus up slick and kill Him.
26.5: But they was like, "Let's not do it during the festival tho, or the people gon' wild out."
26.6: Jesus was chillin' in Bethany at Simon the leper's crib.
26.7: A woman pulled up with a fancy jar full of expensive oil. Sis broke it open and poured it all on His head while He was sittin' at the table.
26.8: The disciples saw that and got tight. They said, "Why she wastin' that?!
26.9: That oil coulda been sold for big money to help the poor."
26.10: But Jesus shut it down. "Why y'all stressin' her? She did somethin' real good for Me.
26.11: The poor gon' always be around, but I won't.
26.12: She poured that oil on Me to get My body ready for burial.
26.13: Believe Me, anywhere the gospel get preached, folks gon' remember her for this."
26.14: Then Judas Iscariot—one of the Twelve—went to the chief priests.
26.15: He said, "What y'all gon' give me if I hand Him over?" They paid him 30 silver coins.
26.16: From then on, Judas was lookin' for his moment to betray Jesus.
26.17: On the first day of the Feast of No-Bread (Unleavened Bread), the disciples came to Jesus like, "Where we fixin' to set up the Passover meal?"
26.18: Jesus told 'em, "Go into the city, find a certain man, and say, 'The Teacher said His time is almost up, and He comin' to eat the Passover at your place with His crew.'"
26.19: So they did exactly what Jesus told 'em and got everything ready.
26.20: That night, Jesus sat down with the Twelve.
26.21: While they was eatin', He hit 'em with: "I'm tellin' y'all straight—one of y'all gon' betray Me."
26.22: They was heartbroken, and each one asked, "Lord… it ain't me, is it?"
26.23: Jesus said, "It's the one who dipped his hand in the dish with Me.
26.24: The Son of Man gon' do what the Scriptures said, but woe to the one who sellin' Me out. It woulda been better if he was never born."
26.25: Then Judas—the one plottin'—asked, "Rabbi… is it me?" Jesus hit him with, "You said it, not me."
26.26: While they was still eatin', Jesus picked up some bread, prayed over it, broke it, and passed it out. "Take this and eat—it's My body."
26.27: Then He grabbed the cup, gave thanks, and passed it too. "Drink up, all y'all.
26.28: This My blood, part of the new promise—poured out for many to forgive sins.
26.29: I ain't drinkin' wine again till we sippin' new in My Father's Kingdom."
26.30: After singin' a song, they dipped out to the Mount of Olives.
26.31: Jesus told 'em, "Tonight, all y'all gon' fall back 'cause of Me. The Scriptures say: 'I'ma strike the Shepherd, and the sheep gon' scatter.'
26.32: But after I rise, I'm meetin' y'all in Galilee."
26.33: Peter was like, "Even if everybody else fold, I ain't goin' out like that!"
26.34: Jesus replied, "Listen close—tonight, before the rooster even crows, you gon' deny Me three times."
26.35: Peter said, "I'll die before I deny You!" And all the other disciples co-signed like, "Us too!"
26.36: Then Jesus took His disciples to a spot called Gethsemane. He told 'em, "Y'all wait here while I go pray over there."
26.37: He took Peter, James, and John with Him, and He started feelin' heavy—real sorrowful, like the weight of the world was sittin' on His chest.
26.38: He told them, "My soul is crushed right now, like I'm 'bout to die. Stay here and keep watch with Me."
26.39: Then He walked a little further, dropped to His knees, face in the dirt, and prayed: "Father, if there's any other way, let this cup pass from Me. But not My will—Yours."
26.40: When He came back, the disciples were knocked out. He said to Peter, "Dang, bruh—you couldn't stay up with Me for one hour?
26.41: Watch and pray, so you don't fall off. The spirit tryin', but the flesh? Weak."
26.42: He dipped again and prayed, "Father, if this the only way, then let it be. I'm wit' it—Your will."
26.43: Came back—they still sleep. Heavy eyes.
26.44: So He went a third time, same prayer.
26.45: Then He came back like, "Y'all still snoozin'? Wake up. The time is now—the Son of Man 'bout to be betrayed.
26.46: Get up. Let's go. My betrayer right around the corner."
26.47: While He was talkin', here come Judas with a mob—swords, clubs, the whole crew sent by the chief priests and elders.
26.48: Judas had told them, "The one I kiss? That's Him. Grab Him."
26.49: He walked up to Jesus all fake—"What's up, Rabbi"—and kissed Him.
26.50: Jesus said, "Go 'head, do what you came to do, friend." Then they grabbed Jesus.
26.51: One of Jesus' people (we know it was Peter) pulled out his sword and sliced a dude's ear off—the servant of the high priest.
26.52: But Jesus told him, "Put that away! If you live by the sword, you gon' die by it.
26.53: You think I can't call My Father and have a whole army of angels show up right now?
26.54: But the Scriptures gotta play out."
26.55: Jesus turned to the mob and said, "Y'all came at Me like I'm some criminal? Swords and clubs? I been in the temple daily teachin', and y'all ain't touch Me.
26.56: But this all had to happen—Scripture said so." And just like that, all His boys dipped. Left Him hangin'.
26.57: The crew that grabbed Jesus dragged Him to Caiaphas, the high priest. The religious leaders were there, already plottin'.
26.58: Peter followed from a distance, slid into the courtyard, and tried to act like he wasn't with Him. Just watchin' to see what would go down.
26.59: The priests and elders tried to stack false charges to kill Jesus, but couldn't get their lies straight.
26.60: Even with a bunch of folks lyin', nothin' stuck. Finally, two stepped up:
26.61: "This Man said He could destroy God's temple and build it back in three days."
26.62: High priest stood up and said, "You ain't got nothin' to say? What about what these men accusin' You of?"
26.63: Jesus stayed silent. Then the high priest pulled the legal card: "I put You under oath. Are You the Christ, the Son of God?"
26.64: Jesus said, "You said it. But let Me tell you—soon you gon' see the Son of Man sittin' next to Power, comin' on the clouds."
26.65: High priest lost it—ripped his robe. "Blasphemy! What else we need? Y'all heard it!"
26.67: Then they spit on Him, punched Him, slapped Him up,
26.68: talkin' reckless: "Oh, you a prophet? Then tell us who hit You!"
26.69: Meanwhile, Peter sittin' outside tryin' to lay low. A servant girl peeped him: "Weren't you with Jesus from Galilee?"
26.70: Peter was like, "Nah, I don't know what you talkin' 'bout."
26.71: He slid out to the gate. Another girl saw him and told the crowd, "He was with Jesus too."
26.72: Peter swore, "I don't know that Man!"
26.73: A few minutes later, some folks came up like, "Yeah, you one of them. We can hear it in your voice."
26.74: Peter lost it—started cursin' and swearin': "I said I don't KNOW that Man!" Right then… rooster crowed.
26.75: Peter remembered Jesus' words: "Before the rooster crows, you'll deny Me three times." And Peter broke down—ran off cryin' hard.

27.1: As soon as the sun came up, the chief priests and elders came up with a whole plot to kill Jesus.
27.2: They tied Him up, marched Him off, and handed Him over to the Roman governor—Pontius Pilate.
27.3: When Judas, the one who snitched, saw that Jesus was really 'bout to die, he started feelin' the weight. He ran it back—tried to return that 30-piece of silver, sayin', "I messed up. I sold out innocent blood."
27.4: But they hit him with, "That ain't our problem. You deal with that."
27.5: So he tossed that silver down in the temple, dipped out… and took his own life.
27.6: The priests picked up the silver like, "We can't put blood money in the offering."
27.7: So they used it to buy a potter's field—a place to bury folks who ain't got nobody.
27.8: That's why folks still call it the "Field of Blood" to this day.
27.9: That prophecy from Jeremiah? Fulfilled right there.
27.10: "And they used that silver to buy the potter's field—just like the Lord told me to do."
27.11: Jesus stood in front of Pilate, who asked, "You the King of the Jews?" Jesus said, "You said it."
27.12: While the priests and elders were throwin' shade and false charges, Jesus said nothing.
27.13: Pilate was like, "You ain't gon' say nothin'? They throwin' all this at you."
27.14: Still—Jesus didn't say a word. Pilate was lowkey shook.
27.15: Now it was a custom for Pilate to release one prisoner during the feast.
27.16: They had a wild dude locked up named Barabbas.
27.17: Pilate asked the crowd, "Y'all want Jesus or Barabbas?"
27.18: (He knew they was just jealous of Jesus.)
27.19: While he was sittin' in the judge's chair, Pilate's wife sent word: "Don't touch that righteous man! I had nightmares 'cause of Him."
27.20: But the priests stirred the crowd—told 'em, "Ask for Barabbas. Get rid of Jesus."
27.21: So Pilate asked again, "Who y'all want?" They yelled, "Barabbas!"
27.22: He said, "Then what y'all want me to do with Jesus?" They yelled, "CRUCIFY HIM!"
27.23: "But what did He even DO?!" They shouted even louder, "CRUCIFY HIM!"
27.24: Pilate saw it was gettin' outta hand, so he washed his hands in front of 'em: "I'm done. This ain't on me. Y'all handle it."
27.25: The crowd said, "His blood be on us and our kids."
27.26: So he let Barabbas go and had Jesus beat… then handed Him over to be crucified.
27.27: The Roman soldiers took Jesus inside, pulled the whole squad up.
27.28: They stripped Him, threw a scarlet robe on Him,
27.29: made a crown outta thorns and shoved it on His head, gave Him a fake scepter, bowed fake like, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
27.30: Then they spit on Him, snatched the reed, and beat Him with it.
27.31: After all that mockin', they put His real clothes back on and dragged Him out to be crucified.
27.32: On the way, they grabbed a man named Simon from Cyrene and made him carry Jesus' cross.
27.33: They reached a spot called Golgotha—means "Skull Place."
27.34: They tried to give Him wine mixed with bitter stuff, but once He tasted it, He wouldn't drink.
27.35: They nailed Him to the cross, divided up His clothes, and gambled for them—just like the Scriptures said.
27.36: Then they just sat there… watchin' Him suffer.
27.37: Over His head they posted the charge: "THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS."
27.38: Two thieves were crucified with Him, one on each side.
27.39: Folks walkin' by were talkin' slick, shakin' their heads.
27.40: "Didn't You say You'd rebuild the temple in 3 days? Save Yourself then! Come off that cross if You the Son of God!"
27.41: The priests and teachers joined in:
27.42: "He saved others, can't save Himself. If You really the King, come down now—we'll believe You then."
27.43: "He trusted God. Let's see if God comes through."
27.44: Even the thieves next to Him were clownin' Him.
27.45: Around noon, darkness hit the land. Stayed dark 'til 3 p.m.
27.46: Then Jesus cried out loud, "Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?" Which means: "My God, My God, why You leave Me hangin'?"
27.47: Some thought He was callin' Elijah.
27.48: Somebody ran and gave Him sour wine on a sponge.
27.49: Others said, "Leave Him alone. Let's see if Elijah comes."
27.50: Then Jesus let out one more loud cry… and gave up His spirit.
27.51: Right then, the temple curtain tore in two—from top to bottom. The earth shook. Rocks cracked.
27.52: Tombs opened up, and saints who had died rose up!
27.53: After Jesus' resurrection, they went into the city and showed up to people!
27.54: The soldier at the cross saw it all and said, "Man… this really was the Son of God."
27.55: A group of women had followed Jesus from Galilee—watched it all go down from a distance.
27.56: Mary Magdalene was there, along with Mary (mother of James and Joses), and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
27.57: That night, a rich dude named Joseph from Arimathea—who was down with Jesus—
27.58: asked Pilate for the body. Pilate agreed.
27.59: Joseph wrapped Jesus in clean linen,
27.60: laid Him in his brand-new tomb, rolled a stone over the entrance, and dipped.
27.61: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary stayed, posted up across from the tomb.
27.62: The next day, the religious leaders ran back to Pilate.
27.63: "Sir, we remember that deceiver said He'd rise after 3 days.
27.64: We need that tomb locked down tight, or else His crew gon' steal the body and fake a resurrection."
27.65: Pilate said, "Fine. Take some guards. Make it as secure as possible."
27.66: So they sealed the tomb… and posted up security.

28.1: Early Sunday mornin', right after the Sabbath, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary pulled up to the tomb.
28.2: All of a sudden, the ground started shakin'—a whole earthquake! An angel straight dropped down from heaven, rolled the stone back, and just sat on it chillin'.
28.3: Dude was shinin' like lightning, clothes white as snow.
28.4: The guards? Shook. Froze up like they were dead.
28.5: The angel looked at the women and said, "Don't be scared. I know y'all lookin' for Jesus, the One they crucified.
28.6: He ain't here—He done got up, just like He said He would. Come see where He was layin'.
28.7: Now go! Quick! Tell His boys He alive and already headed to Galilee. You gon' see Him there. I done told y'all!"
28.8: The women ran up outta there—heart poundin', eyes wide—but filled with so much joy. They ran to tell the disciples the news.
28.9: On the way, Jesus popped up on them like, "Y'all rejoice now!" They dropped to His feet and started worshippin' Him.
28.10: He said, "Don't be scared. Go tell My brothers to meet Me in Galilee. I'll see them there."
28.11: While the women were movin', some of the guards ran to the city to spill everything to the religious leaders.
28.12: The priests and elders held a hush-hush meeting and came up with a bribe plan.
28.13: They handed the soldiers a fat bag of money and said, "Tell folks His disciples came in the night and stole the body while y'all were asleep.
28.14: If the governor hears about it, we'll cover for y'all. Don't trip."
28.15: So the guards took the cash and stuck to the script. And that's the story folks been passin' around ever since.
28.16: Meanwhile, the eleven disciples headed up to that mountain in Galilee—just like Jesus told 'em.
28.17: When they saw Him, they fell down in worship… though a few still had doubts in their hearts.
28.18: Then Jesus stepped up and said, "All power in heaven and on earth? That's Mine now.
28.19: So go—make disciples everywhere, all nations. Baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
28.20: Teach 'em everything I taught y'all. And don't forget—I'm with y'all. Always. Even to the very end."
